root_idea.summary: The root centers on opening, spreading, and making something apparent; its communicative extension is clarification and exposition.
root_idea.development: The semantic orientation is described from spreading or cutting meat, developing into opening or laying things bare, explaining what is obscure, and, in Quranic usage, expanding the breast for receptivity.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The group is a Quran-attested Form I verb and is presented under the normalized perfect-tense citation form.

senses.definition: To open or expand the breast, making it receptive to a matter.
senses.usage_conditions: Used in the Quranic chest or breast construction for receptivity and acceptance, including receptivity to Islam or truth and, in 16:106, to disbelief. The same sense may be rendered as “open,” “expand,” or “dilate.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: To uncover, lay open, expose, display, reveal, or disclose something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of making a thing visible or an affair apparent.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To explain, expound, interpret, or make clear an affair, question, obscure matter, tradition, or discourse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An explanatory and interpretive use applied to matters whose meaning is hidden or requires clarification.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To open, widen, or dilate a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A general physical opening or expansion use, distinct from the Quranic chest construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To deflower or have sexual intercourse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A sexual construction describing intercourse or defloration.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To manifest desire or become expansive in one's desire toward something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative construction expressing eagerness or strong desire.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cut flesh-meat lengthwise or into thin oblong slices.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The lexical descriptions also include cutting meat from a joint or on the bone; the related Form II can indicate cutting it into many such pieces.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To understand speech or language.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A use describing comprehension rather than explanation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Keeping, preserving, or guarding.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized use particularly associated with guarding seed-produce from birds.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To expound, explain, or interpret language or discourse thoroughly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The intensive Form II expression is used for detailed exposition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To dissect or anatomize a body.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical physical use of the intensive form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For the breast or bosom to become expanded and receptive.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The inchoative or reflexive construction may describe expansion with joy or receptivity to Islam.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To ask for language or discourse to be expounded, explained, or interpreted.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A request for someone to provide an explanation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To ask for flesh-meat to be cut in the manner called شَرْح.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A request construction referring to the preparation of meat in slices.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A full exposition, explanation, or running commentary on a work.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical literary term for a commentary covering the text as a whole, distinguished from a حاشية that comments on particular words or passages.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A piece or thin slice of flesh-meat cut into an oblong form.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term can denote meat prepared in the cutting manner called شَرْح.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The discovery, disclosure, or explanation of an affair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used as a noun for making an affair known or intelligible.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cut of flesh-meat, especially one cut into oblong slices.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An attributive or nominal description of meat prepared by slicing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The vulva.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical noun, also recorded as a proper name for the same organ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cut piece or thin slice of flesh-meat, including an extended piece of fatty meat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural is شَرَائِحُ; the term denotes meat cut into slices.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An expositor, explainer, or interpreter of a book or similar work.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An active-participial noun for a person who provides explanation or interpretation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A keeper or guardian.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A dialectal specialization, particularly in Yemen, for a guardian of seed-produce from birds.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The anus.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The cited lexical description specifies the lower opening of a man.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A mirage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate nominal usage, with مَسْرُوحٌ recorded as a dialectal variant.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Widening or dilation is covered by the broader opening sense.
Quranic breast expansion and a separate desire construction.
Requests for explanation or meat preparation.
Identifies the verbal noun without adding a lexical branch.
Slice or cut piece of meat.

cautions: All five Quranic occurrences are Form I uses in a chest or breast construction; the broader Classical meanings are not additional Quranic senses.

The older citation notation associated with the Lane chest discussion is not used as a modern verse locator; Quran locations here follow secure QAC locations and the explicitly supplied Quran-focused evidence.
